Question B-006-004-007.

Why the correct answer is right: On HF, open-wire line has very low loss because much of its field is in air and conductor losses are small when it is installed clear of nearby objects. It is the lowest-loss option listed.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "75-ohm twin-lead": Twin-lead has more dielectric around the conductors and is not the lowest-loss HF line in the list.
- sourceIndex 2: "coaxial cable": Coax is convenient and shielded, but its dielectric and conductor losses are generally higher than well-installed open-wire line on HF.
- sourceIndex 3: "300-ohm twin-lead": 300-ohm twin-lead can be useful, yet open-wire line with wider air spacing is the lower-loss choice here.
